title: Perpetual check across a reveal: the checking side loses at the third occurrence

boundary.expect: second occurrence of the checking position; not yet terminal

rationale: The first ply is a reveal: the piece on a1 is face down, moves as the chariot whose square it is, and arrives on a10 face up and giving check. Everything after it is one cycle — the chariot alternates a10 and a9, checking after every Red move, while the general shuttles e10 and e9 and never attacks anything — and the checking position stands at plies 1, 5 and 9. On the third occurrence the violation is complete and the side giving the checks loses, exactly as xq-chk-001 has it, the two games adjudicating repetition identically because this game's rules adopt those clauses whole. The reveal is what this fixture adds: it lies before every repeated position, which is not an accident of the line but the rule — a hidden piece stands only on its own start square and flips the moment it moves, so the face-down set only ever shrinks and no repeating cycle can contain a reveal.
